action: Tsume customers: change your Tsume password and any other account that reuses it, and treat emails or calls about extra payments or pre-order changes as suspect; contact info@tsume-art.com to check.
date_note: Date the company says it detected the intrusion; the report was published 19 November.
exec: A collectibles retailer says someone reached its management system for about five weeks; customer contact details and order histories may be exposed.
geo_basis: country (company is Luxembourg-based; city not stated)
plain: Tsume, a Luxembourg maker of collectible anime figures, told customers an outsider got into its management system and may have seen names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and past orders. It says payment data is not affected.
summary: Cyberattaque.org reports, from a customer email it obtained, that Tsume says an outsider accessed its management system between 9 October and 16 November 2026. Tsume says it detected this on 16 November and closed access within two hours. Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and order histories may be exposed; Tsume says payment data is not affected and has notified Luxembourg's CNPD.
title: Luxembourg figurine maker Tsume says outsider accessed its management system for about five weeks

validation.note: Single publisher (Cyberattaque.org) relaying a customer email from Tsume; Tsume's own notice not found online and no second publisher located.

key_findings: Access to the management system between 9 October and 16 November 2026, detected on 16 November and closed in under two hours, per Tsume's email as reported.
Data possibly exposed: names, postal addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and past order histories; no evidence yet that it was viewed or copied.
Payment data not affected; breach reported to the CNPD; no attribution or claim identified.
recommendations: Change the password at next login and on any service reusing it.
Be wary of messages impersonating Tsume asking for extra payments.
